title: A Unified Framework for Image-to-3D Part Generation via Variable Granularity
claim: Separate specialized models handle each control granularity; one unified model accepts all of them and produces high-quality outputs.
layout: 2 panels; left unified-vs-separate diagram flowing top to bottom, right sample gallery
description: Two panels. Panel (a), on the left, uses a submarine example. Across the top, three conditioning inputs sit in funnel-shaped beams: sparse points ("rapid indication"), bounding boxes ("rough layout") and segmentation masks ("precise shape"). Arrows from the points and masks, plus a green arrow from the boxes, converge on a blue rounded box labelled "Unified Generator (ours)". Brown arrows lead from that box down to three part-colored submarine meshes. Below each mesh is a green box (Point-based, Box-based, Mask-based Model), and a "Separated Methods" box groups these three as the prior approach. Panel (b), on the right, is a 3×5 gallery of pastel part-colored 3D assets: robots, a monster, a house, vases, a pirate figure, a swan, a tray and guns. Gradient titles head both panels. The eye goes first to the colorful submarine and the central generator box.
caption: (a) Our unified framework integrates variable-granularity geometric prompts from sparse points to dense masks into one model for flexible part control. (b) The proposed method produces high-fidelity, semantically coherent 3D parts across diverse object categories.
abstract: Controllable 3D part generation is pivotal for digital asset creation, yet existing methods lack the flexibility to accommodate diverse user workflows requiring varying levels of control. In this paper, we introduce FlexPart, a unified image-to-3D part generation framework that supports variable-granularity geometric conditions within a single model. By seamlessly integrating heterogeneous inputs, ranging from sparse points to dense bounding boxes and masks, via gated adaptive modulation, FlexPart unlocks a powerful cross-modal synergy. We also propose an asymmetric geometric guidance mechanism that leverages strong spatial priors to align representations across granularities, improving geometric consistency and facilitating inter-task synergy. Under mask conditioning on PartVerseXL, FlexPart reduces Part CD by 16.6% relative to TripoSG + SAM3D and by 10.5% relative to OmniPart, while maintaining competitive whole-mesh quality. The code can be found at https://github.com/Gucci233/FlexPart
